title-group.article-title: Synthetic Field-Dependent Carrier Mobility in Amorphous Semiconductors

sec.title: 1. Model
sec.p: Charge transport in amorphous semiconductors is described by the drift diffusion framework. The diffusion coefficient D= μkBT q relates to the mobility μ through the Einstein relation, where kB is the Boltzmann constant (8.617×10−5 eV/K), T is the absolute temperature, taken as T = 300 K throughout this synthetic example, and q is the elementary charge (1.602×10−19 C).

Above the Poole–Frenkel onset field, the mobility follows (2)
μ(E) =μ0 exp(β E) where E is the electric field strength in V cm−1, μ0 is the zero-field mobility (4×10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1 here), and β is the Poole–Frenkel coefficient, β = 2×10−3 (V cm−1)−1/2.

sec.title: 2. Consistency check
sec.p: Equation (1) is recovered when the electric field vanishes, since exp(0) = 1 and the zero-field mobility μ0 enters the Einstein relation directly. Substituting μ0 = 4×10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1 into Equation (1) at T = 300 K yields D = 1.03×10−5 cm2 s−1, the value reported in Table 1.
